full_judgment:
5. Plaintiff filed Mis. Case 27 of 1989 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside that order of suit to its file and number. The miscellaneous case was contested by the defendant. An affidavit was sworn, in support of the application of the plaintiff filed under Order 9 rule 4 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 6. Trial Court dismissed the Misc Case finding, inter alia, that by order dated 27-7-1989, a last chance was given to the plaintiff for taking necessary step for getting the thumb impression of the defendant 3 to be examined by an expert but plaintiff did not take any step. 

 Here in this case, on the relevant date, the plaintiff was not absent from the court, but he made an application praying for issuance of warrant of arrest against the defendant No.3 for the aforesaid purpose, Therefore, after rejecting the application for issuance of warrant, without passing further order directing the parties to get ready passing of the order of dismissal of the suit is hit by Order 9 rule 3 of the Code. It is held that a suit cannot be dismissed order 9 rule 3 of the Code. When the plaintiff made an application in the court, as referred above treating the position as absence of the plaintiff, which is apparently illegal. So dismissal of the suit on that count is not tenable in the eye of law. He further submits that according to the provision of Order 16 rule 10(1)(3) of the Code, the trial Court should issue a warrant of arrest for production of the defendant No. 3.
